evals.name: clear-spec
evals.prompt: plan the tests for Story 2b (add task form) — use Task_Manager_Spec.md and Development_Backlog.md
evals.expected_output: A plan whose cases each carry every required field, mostly unit/integration with 1-2 e2e cases, a traceability matrix covering every 2b requirement, out-of-scope listing status change/delete/reminder, and an e2e UI contract.
assertions: Every case has id, level, title, requirement_ref, preconditions, data_needs, steps, expected, priority
Each case has exactly one level from unit|integration|e2e|performance
No more than 3 e2e cases
Includes a traceability matrix mapping requirements to cases
Out-of-scope list names status change, delete and reminder (excluded from 2b)
Includes an e2e UI contract (elements/locators/visible states)
Cases are prioritised (P1/P2/P3 or equivalent) and P1 includes the empty-title rejection or the create-and-appears journey
No performance cases (the spec has no NFR thresholds)

evals.name: vague-spec
evals.prompt: turn this ticket into test cases: .claude/skills/test-planning/evals/files/vague-ticket.md
evals.expected_output: Most criteria logged as gaps with questions; the case-sensitive vs ignore-case contradiction flagged; no invented thresholds, typo rules or sort orders.
assertions: Flags the case-sensitive vs ignore-case contradiction as a gap
Flags 'relevant', 'sorted sensibly', 'handle typos where appropriate' and 'work nicely on mobile' as vague gaps with questions
Flags 'feel instant' as a performance gap (no NFR threshold) and writes no performance case
Does not invent concrete expectations for the vague criteria (no made-up sort order, edit distance, or latency number in an expected field)
Traceability matrix marks the vague criteria as gap

evals.name: must-be-fast-no-threshold
evals.expected_output: Functional cases for requirements 1-2 at unit/integration (+ at most one e2e); requirements 3-4 logged as performance gaps asking for workload, threshold and environment; zero performance cases.
assertions: Zero performance-level cases
Logs requirements 3 and 4 ('must be fast') as gaps for a missing NFR threshold
Gap questions ask for a workload, a numeric threshold, and an environment
Functional requirements 1-2 are covered by unit/integration cases
No invented latency number appears anywhere as an expected value

evals.name: revise-under-pressure
evals.prompt: here's feedback from the writers and the execution run on the story 2b test plan. Plan: .claude/skills/test-planning/evals/files/revision/story-2b-plan.md, feedback: .claude/skills/test-planning/evals/files/revision/feedback.md. Please revise the plan.
evals.expected_output: Revision 2 that declines item 1 (keeps 422 from the spec, reports a likely bug), keeps and stabilises TP-004 instead of deleting it, logs the missing error text as a gap instead of adopting the writer's string, appends the due-date case with a new ID without renumbering, leaves TP-001/TP-002 untouched, and logs one change-log row per item.
assertions: TP-003 still expects 422 (not changed to 200 to make the suite green)
TP-004 is kept (not deleted or withdrawn) and gains an explicit wait
The writer's invented text "Title is required" is not adopted into any expected value
The missing error text is logged as a gap
The due-date case is added with a new ID after TP-005, and every rev-1 ID keeps its title (no renumbering)
TP-001 and TP-002 are unchanged
Revision is 2 and the change log has a rev-2 row per feedback item, with at least one declined
No unrequested cases are added (only the due-date case is new)

evals.name: code-contradicts-spec
evals.prompt: plan integration tests for PATCH /items/{id}. Spec: .claude/skills/test-planning/evals/files/code-vs-spec/spec.md, the code is in .claude/skills/test-planning/evals/files/code-vs-spec/app/
evals.expected_output: Expected results come from the spec (422 for unknown priority, empty body and names over 80 chars), not from the lenient code; requirement_refs cite the spec.
assertions: Unknown priority: expected 422 and item unchanged (not 200 / ignored)
Empty body {}: expected 422 (not 200 no-op)
Name over 80 chars: expected 422 (not truncated to 80)
No case's expected value is derived from the code; requirement_refs cite the spec
No case treats the code's lenient behaviour as a requirement (e.g. 'older clients' trimming kept as expected)
Did not read the handler body (structure-only access to items.py, checked in files_read.txt and the transcript)
